note: Item text and option anchors transcribed verbatim from the S1 File's SPSS variable labels and value labels (haven::read_sav). The IRW item codes ARE the source column names -- data/mohammed_2021_patient_safety.py melts JOBSAT_ITEMS = ['jobsat','jobsats','jobsatss','jobsatsss','jobsatssss'] directly with var_name='item' -- so the code-to-text tie is mechanical, with no positional or order inference (core model pattern 1). Text is NOT normalised: the source labels are all lowercase, carry no terminal punctuation, and jobsatsss reads 'am proud to work at this hospital' with no leading 'I'; all five are shipped exactly as they appear in the file. Anchors 1='strongly disagree' to 5='strongly agree' come from FIVE separate SPSS value-label sets (labels53-labels57), one per item, whose contents are identical -- so the agreement is a property of the data rather than of a shared pointer (asserted per item in the build script and re-checked per item in step 2 of the verify script). Correction from Ben, issue #1696. The paper (10.1371/journal.pone.0245966) never reproduces these five items and never names the instrument -- its only mention of job satisfaction is a dichotomous Table 1 covariate. Identification as the SAQ Job Satisfaction domain rests on the wording matching that domain's five items (SAQ short form items 15-19, per uth.edu/chqs), with 'hospital' substituted for 'office'; it is not stated by the study. instructions left NA: the article's only Supporting Information is the .sav, so administered instruction text is not recoverable. Anchor DIRECTION could not be corroborated independently, for reasons unrelated to the item text: the file's derived Jobsatisfaction variable (279 not satisfied / 132 satisfied, matching Table 1) is uncorrelated with the five items (point-biserial 0.035, no threshold beats the 67.9% base rate), so it is a separate self-report and not a composite of them; and the five items are uncorrelated with all 81 other variables in the file (max |r| 0.091, median 0.022) where the HSOPSC block reaches 0.85. Direction therefore rests on the value labels alone. SEPARATE RESPONSE-DATA OBSERVATIONS, not item-text issues and not yet raised with Ben (Xingyi is reviewing them first): (a) the file carries a periodic exact-duplicate structure that is FILE-WIDE, not specific to this table -- the 42-item HSOPSC pattern is exactly reproduced 130 rows later for 31.0% of rows (270 distinct patterns / 411 respondents), which cannot occur by chance for 42 values, and the jobsat block does the same at lag 39 for 46.5% of rows (91 distinct / 411). Comparable 5-item HSOPSC blocks show exact repeats of 44-54% at lag 130, so the jobsat rate is NOT elevated relative to genuine blocks; an earlier framing of lag 39 as jobsat-specific compared a 5-column block against a single column and was withdrawn. No full records are duplicated (411/411 distinct). This bears on mohammed_2021_patient_safety_culture at least as much as on this table. (b) What is specific to the jobsat block: it is correlationally isolated -- max |r| of its 5-item mean with any of the 81 other file variables is 0.091, where the HSOPSC positive block reaches 0.848 -- and 55.7% of respondents gave all five items the same answer against 12-22% for genuine 5-item HSOPSC blocks. Section 6 of verify_mohammed_2021_job_satisfaction.R reproduces both.
